science.title: Network analysis of physical activity, exercise health beliefs, and three dimensions of the good life: identifying central and bridge nodes
science.description: Positive psychology has typically examined subjective well-being, meaning in life, and psychological richness as separate outcomes, leaving unclear how these dimensions of the good life relate to physical activity and exercise-specific health beliefs within a common system. This cross-sectional study estimated an 11-node regularised partial-correlation network from a Spearman correlation matrix among 673 Chinese college students. The nodes represented physical activity, six dimensions of exercise health beliefs, and four observed indicators spanning the three dimensions of the good life: subjective well-being, presence of meaning, search for meaning, and psychological richness. Expected influence (EI) quantified each node’s overall signed connectivity, whereas bridge expected influence (Bridge EI) quantified signed connectivity across five prespecified theoretical communities. Edge-weight accuracy and the case-dropping stability of EI and Bridge EI were assessed using bootstrap procedures, and alternative community partitions were examined in sensitivity analyses. The estimated network was characterised predominantly by positive conditional associations. Presence of meaning showed the highest EI, followed by psychological richness and perceived exercise benefits. Under the a priori five-community specification, psychological richness, presence of meaning, and subjective well-being showed the highest Bridge EI values. The bridge ranking of psychological richness declined under alternative partitions, whereas presence of meaning remained comparatively prominent across specifications. EI and Bridge EI both demonstrated high case-dropping stability (correlation-stability coefficient = 0.75 for each). These findings position the presence of meaning as the most broadly connected node in the estimated network and show that conclusions about psychological richness as a statistical bridge depend partly on community definition. The results generate hypotheses concerning meaning-oriented and experientially varied physical-activity components, but longitudinal studies are needed to establish temporal ordering, and experimental studies are needed to determine whether incorporating such components produces changes in connected outcomes.

science.title: Green synthesis of CuO nanoparticles using mangrove leaves for targeted delivery of platinum (II) therapeutics
science.description: Copper oxide nanoparticles (CuO NPs) synthesized via green chemistry using Avicennia marina mangrove leaf extract represent an environmentally sustainable approach to generating biocompatible nanomaterials for pharmaceutical applications. This study utilized the phytochemical-rich extract as both a reducing and capping agent to produce quasi-spherical monoclinic CuO NPs with a diameter range of 35–87 nm. The resulting nanoparticles possessed a specific surface area of 4.5 m² g⁻¹ with a mesoporous structure (pore volume of 0.018 cm³ g⁻¹), making them ideal candidates for drug loading applications. The CuO NPs were subsequently evaluated as nanocarriers for two clinically relevant platinum (II) chemotherapeutics: cisplatin and oxaliplatin. Characterization via Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy confirmed successful coordination of platinum drug ligands to surface Cu/O sites, while Brunauer–Emmett–Teller analysis demonstrated a substantial decrease in surface area upon drug loading, indicating effective pore occupancy. Cisplatin demonstrated an entrapment efficiency of 28% with a loading capacity of 56 mg/g, while oxaliplatin exhibited comparable loading performance. The in vitro release profiles of cisplatin and oxaliplatin from mangrove-derived green CuO NPs show sustained release, with cisplatin reaching 70% cumulative release within 20 h and oxaliplatin approaching 80% in the same period. The release kinetics follow first-order behavior for cisplatin and Higuchi model for oxaliplatin, indicating that release is predominantly governed by diffusion from the mesoporous CuO matrix. These findings establish mangrove-derived CuO nanoparticles as a promising carrier for sustainable platinum-based drug delivery, offering an environmentally friendly approach and enhanced therapeutic potential while eliminating the need for toxic precursors and energy-intensive conventional synthesis methods.

science.title: Differentiation of clear cell and non clear cell renal cell carcinoma through high-frame-rate contrast-enhanced ultrasound
science.description: To evaluate the value of high-frame-rate contrast-enhanced ultrasound (H-CEUS) in differentiating between clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) and non-clear cell renal cell carcinoma (nccRCC). A retrospective study was conducted on 84 patients diagnosed with CCRCC and 28 patients diagnosed with nccRCC, all patients underwent conventional ultrasound (US), conventional contrast-enhanced ultrasound (C-CEUS), and High-frame-rate contrast-enhanced ultrasound (H-CEUS) at the First Affiliated Hospital of Nanchang University between October 2022 and April 2024. Dynamic image sequences were acquired for each patient. Clinical, US, C-CEUS, and H-CEUS parameters were compared between the two groups using t-tests, χ² tests, Fisher’s exact tests, and U-tests as appropriate. Binary logistic regression was employed to identify independent risk factors associated with ccRCC and nccRCC, combining clinical, US, C-CEUS, and H-CEUS data. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was performed to assess the diagnostic accuracy of C-CEUS and H-CEUS. Nomograms were constructed using R to visualize the probability of ccRCC based on significant parameters. Significant differences were observed between ccRCC and nccRCC groups in color Doppler flow imaging (CDFI) patterns (χ²=10.967, p = 0.012). Analysis of contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) characteristics revealed significant differences between the two groups in terms of enhancement mode, regression mode, peak intensity, homogeneity, and presence of no enhancement for both H-CEUS and C-CEUS (all p < 0.05). Time-intensity curve (TIC) parameter analysis showed that time to peak (TTP) was shorter in the ccRCC group compared to the nccRCC group for both H-CEUS and C-CEUS (Z = 3.434, 2.355; p = 0.001, = 0.019). Conversely, time to decline (DT/2) and mean transit time (MTT) were longer in the ccRCC group for both H-CEUS and C-CEUS (Z = 3.749, 3.649; p < 0.001, < 0.001 in H-CEUS; Z = 3.407, 3.239; p = 0.001, = 0.001 in C-CEUS). Peak intensity (PI) and area under the curve (AUC) were also higher in the ccRCC group for both H-CEUS and C-CEUS (Z = 3.007, 4.173; p = 0.003, < 0.001 in H-CEUS; Z = 3.897, 3.911; p < 0.001, < 0.001 in C-CEUS). Binary logistic regression analysis identified regression mode, homogeneity, and TTP of H-CEUS as independent risk factors for differentiating ccRCC from nccRCC. ROC curve analysis demonstrated superior diagnostic performance of H-CEUS compared to C-CEUS, with a sensitivity of 81.0%, specificity of 89.3%, and an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.935. For C-CEUS, peak intensity, homogeneity, and PI were identified as independent risk factors. ROC curve analysis showed a sensitivity of 69.1%, a specificity of 87.5%, and an AUC of 0.784. Statistical analysis confirmed that H-CEUS had significantly higher diagnostic efficiency than C-CEUS (Z=-2.892, p = 0.004). Nomograms were constructed using R language to visually represent the probability of ccRCC based on significant C-CEUS and H-CEUS parameters. H-CEUS, with its improved time resolution, shows potential for enhancing diagnostic differentiation between ccRCC and nccRCC. This technology may provide a valuable tool for the precise diagnosis of renal cell carcinoma.

science.title: Enhancing protein structure prediction accuracy by prioritizing important residues using protein language models
science.description: Accurate prediction of protein tertiary structures from amino acid sequences remains a fundamental challenge in computational biology. Although AlphaFold2 represents a major advance, systematic discrepancies persist between its predictions and experimentally determined structures. Given that individual residues contribute differentially to protein function, we hypothesize that incorporating residue-specific importance metrics improves prediction accuracy. Here, we develop i-Fold (importance Fold), an enhanced neural architecture that builds upon the AlphaFold2 framework by integrating protein language model-derived residue importance scores as dynamic positional weights during training. Evaluation on a benchmark test set of 3599 protein structures reveals that the prediction error of i-Fold is reduced by 0.3 Å on average, improving the prediction success rate by 7.6%, and consistent results are obtained on an independent test set of 167 recently released protein structures. Notably, i-Fold demonstrates particular improvements for targets that are typically challenging for AlphaFold2, including ribosomal proteins, membrane proteins, and orphan proteins. Our findings indicate that explicit integration of evolutionary residue importance can advance the state-of-the-art in protein structure prediction, producing more accurate and generalizable models without substantially increasing computational cost. The i-Fold architecture integrates language modelderived residue importance scores to guide AlphaFold2, significantly improving structure prediction accuracy and resolving topological bottlenecks in flexible protein regions.
